ad313b76a687a701: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Serian remains under the haze emergency despite its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading improving from the hazardous level, with the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) continuing to closely monitor the situation.

SDMC chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said in a statement today that the Serian air quality monitoring station recorded an API reading of 334 as at 10am, placing the area in the hazardous category.
However, the reading fell to 273 by 2pm, bringing it into the very unhealthy category.
He said SDMC would monitor the API reading over the next three days to observe any fluctuations, particularly the possibility of it rising above 500.
“The API is primarily affected by the wind direction and source of hotspots,” he said.
Uggah said the monitoring would be carried out before any recommendation was made to the Sarawak Premier and Prime Minister regarding the status of the emergency in Serian.

Yesterday, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim consented to the declaration of an emergency in the Serian Division following worsening haze that had pushed air pollution to hazardous levels, with API readings exceeding 500.

The Prime Minister’s Office, in a statement yesterday, said the decision was made after taking into consideration the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Sarawak Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and relevant agencies monitoring air quality in the affected area.
Although Serian remains under the emergency, Uggah said government and private offices, as well as other workplaces in the affected area, may continue operating.
This includes industries, plantations, construction sites and quarries.
“However, they must take health precautionary measures,” he said.
Uggah said SDMC was also closely monitoring air quality, weather conditions, hotspots and haze movement across Sarawak so that appropriate action could be taken as the situation develops.
The public was advised to avoid outdoor activities, while those who could not avoid exposure outdoors were advised to wear an N95 mask or, at minimum, a three-ply mask.
Uggah also urged the public to take particular care of children, senior citizens and other vulnerable groups who may be more affected by the haze.
He said SDMC would continue to monitor the situation closely and issue further updates as necessary.
The committee would also continue working closely with relevant State and Federal agencies to manage the situation.
“The health, safety and wellbeing of the people of Sarawak remain our highest priority,” he said. — The Borneo Post
ed09dac2eb780f9c: PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department will intensify enforcement operations to track down foreigners holding more than 1,300 Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) believed to have been irregularly approved through a syndicate uncovered under Op Crack.

Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department's enforcement division was also gathering intelligence on the ground to identify and locate foreigners holding the improperly approved passes.
"We will continue carrying out enforcement operations to trace the holders of PLKS that were approved irregularly.
"There are at least 1,300 of these PLKS which are believed to be in the hands of foreigners after being issued through the syndicate.
"We will either catch them through intelligence gathered or through targeted operations," he told the New Straits Times.
Zakaria said the department also welcomed information from the public that could assist enforcement officers in locating foreigners holding the irregularly approved PLKS.
He said information received would help the department identify and track down those who had benefited from the syndicate's activities.
"Rest assured that the identities of those who come forward with information would be kept strictly confidential," he said.
It was previously reported that immigration officers attempting to track down holders of the irregularly issued PLKS hit a snag after finding that their registered addresses were also fake.
The department conducted several raids at addresses linked to the affected permits as part of ongoing investigations.
However, officers found that the information registered under the permits did not correspond with the actual locations.
Zakaria said then that although their system contained certain addresses, officers found different premises when they visited the locations, while the employer information also did not match.

The department had earlier said it would cancel all improperly approved PLKS and trace their holders following the dismantling of a syndicate suspected of hacking the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to manipulate the pass approval process.

Zakaria had said the move was the first step following the discovery of PLKS approvals that did not comply with procedures during Op Crack, a joint operation between the Immigration Department and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
It was previously reported that 12 individuals, including six Immigration Department personnel and a police officer, were detained by the MACC for allegedly being involved in the syndicate.
Investigations found that 1,306 PLKS were allegedly approved through unused foreign-worker quotas, resulting in an estimated RM2.4 million in lost levy payments.
Nine bank accounts containing about RM300,000 were also reportedly frozen as part of the investigation.
b4ab849d48297b03: JAKARTA: An orangutan mother and her baby, threatened by encroaching wildfires to their habitat in Indonesia, were rescued earlier this week, authorities said in a statement Saturday.

The vast Southeast Asian archipelago has for weeks been fighting wildfires blanketing parts of Borneo and Sumatra with smog, with haze also contributing to air pollution in Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.
The orangutan pair had been under observation since July after being spotted in a plantation area near a forest in West Kalimantan, a local natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.
But authorities decided to evacuate them to a rescue center managed by the wildlife foundation Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) on Thursday as fire spread near their habitat.
Their health is being closely monitored by veterinarians, but a preliminary check found no burn injuries on the two great apes.

"Exposure to smoke over a period of time... can affect the orangutan's respiratory system, especially when smoke concentrations in the habitat are very high," YIARI's veterinarian Komara, who like many Indonesians uses only one name, said in a statement.
"Both individuals will continue to be monitored while they are at the rescue and rehabilitation center."

The latest rescue means nine orangutans have been evacuated because of threats from wildfires in less than a month in the Ketapang district of West Kalimantan province, YIARI operational director Argitoe Ranting said.
"This shows that fires not only destroy forests but also deprive animals of shelter and food," Argitoe said.
Most animals "do not have many options" to relocate as their habitat burns, he added.

One orangutan died after being rescued last week, with a necropsy result pointing to smoke exposure as the cause of death, the West Kalimantan natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.

811b0d9c7fb52cc3: "THE struggle behind the collapse and rebuilding of community – which is the foundation of daily life – resonates with people today surrounded by uncertainty, while also delivering a gust of positivity," says director Lee Sang-Il.
He is referring to his 2006 film, 'Hula Girls', screened in a 4K remastered version as part of the Japanese Film Festival line-up for this year under the Japan Foundation.
Set in a declining Japanese mining town, 'Hula Girl's follows a group of young women who learn the Hawaiian hula to help revitalise their community.
It won several awards, including the Japanese Academy's Best Film award in 2007.
The 52-year-old says audiences might also find 'Hula Girls' interesting after all these years due to the popularity of his most recent film, 'Kokuho'.
The latter, which won the Japanese Academy's 2026 Best Film and Best Director awards, is about a gangster family-born boy who finds himself adopted by a kabuki actor.
'Kokuho', Japan's 2026 Oscar submission, will have a special screening on Sept 9 at GSC MidValley and GSC MyTown in Kuala Lumpur.
"Although there is a difference in degree, perhaps many audiences find meaning in the shared theme of unwavering focus of a person dedicating their life to art," says Lee.
Having also won awards for his screenplays, Lee says he has never considered releasing books to go with his movies.

"I'm conscious of the fact that my sensibilities are best suited for converting written word into images. For example, a long verbal exchange in a novel might be conveyed without a word being said, just by the atmosphere between the actors or some imagery. And conversely, the invisible emotions buried between lines of text could be given shape by an image.
"It's because I firmly believe my abilities can be best used to show through interpretation a different facet of a character, or unearthing a lode buried within the story."
The acclaimed film director says he gets a sense of fulfilment from filmmaking.

"There was nothing else that I liked. Meaning, I like films. If I were shooting a film, one naturally feels it upon completion, but there's an additional sense of achievement when it reaches an audience, and sometimes it may reach viewers overseas, like this time. The high I get is difficult to get elsewhere."

Lee's 'Hula Girls' is part of JFF's Girl Power selection, movies inspired by real-life events. The other two films in this section are ''Fujiko' and 'Purehearted'. 'Fujiko', a 2026 movie, was screened at the JFF press conference in mid-August.

It is about a young woman who fights to get her daughter back and raises her as a single mother. Interestingly, director Taichi Kimura has incorporated J-rock and psychedelic rock into the film score.

JFF pays tribute to Yamada Yoji, celebrating 65 years of his contribution to cinema. The 95-year-old filmmaker will have four of his films featured – 'Tokyo Taxi', 'A Distant Cry from Spring', Tora-san's 'Many Splintered Love' and 'Renjishi' (The Father and Son Shishi Lions).

Another highlight is Akira Kurosawa's classic 'Throne of Blood' (1957), an adaptation of Shakespeare's 'Macbeth', which remains one of the most acclaimed Japanese interpretations of the classic tragedy.
The festival this year presents a total of 15 films. They include the anime 'Chimney Town: Frozen in Time', 'One Last Love Letter', and 'Samurai Vengeance'.
The festival runs Sept 8 to Oct 18, travelling to GSC cinemas in five states, including Klang Valley, Penang (Sept 17-20), Johor Baru (Sept 24-27), Kuching (Oct 8-11) and Kota Kinabalu (Oct 15-18).
Visit GSC or Japan Foundation websites for more details.

b223dd714593dd3a: KUALA LUMPUR: Chemical emissions from industries, vehicle exhaust fumes, as well as water and soil pollution can no longer be regarded solely as environmental issues, as prolonged exposure has been linked to various cancers, including among children.

Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said cancer prevention efforts should not focus solely on factors such as smoking and diet, but also address chemicals released by factories, vehicle emissions and other pollutants children may inhale or be exposed to daily.
He said the issue represented a gap that was not discussed often enough, despite the potential harm caused by environmental exposure.
"It sits in the shadows behind many of the cancer cases that fill our hospitals: the air our children breathe and the harm that too often is caused by what is hidden within it."
Sultan Nazrin said this at the launch of the National Cancer Congress Malaysia 2026 and the coffee table book, A Breath For The Future: Malaysia's National Lung Health Initiative.

He said the concern was particularly pertinent given the difficult environmental conditions affecting the region, including forest fires in Kalimantan, a dry season intensified by El Nino and winds blowing in an unfavourable direction for Malaysia.
He also urged Malaysia to take note of the emergence of so-called "cancer alleys", where heavy industry had grown faster than safeguards intended to protect nearby communities.

Citing communities in Louisiana in the United States, industrial areas in South Africa and China, and the Niger Delta in West Africa, where concerns had emerged over cancer risks associated with industrial activity and pollution, he said Malaysia should regard such examples as a warning.

"This is not a problem unique to any one country or industry and it is a pattern we in Malaysia, with our own industrial corridors and our own rivers running past factories and plantations, would be wise to take as a caution rather than a distant headline."

Sultan Nazrin also highlighted a documentary about a community in southern Iraq living near intensive oil and gas extraction, where routine gas flaring exposed residents to potentially harmful chemicals and children reportedly experienced unusually high rates of leukaemia.
He said the example illustrated the broader health risks posed by pollution, noting that scientists had learned over many years that pollution did not only harm the lungs.

"Chemicals released by industry, by traffic and by the fuels we burn to run both have been linked to childhood leukaemia and to cancers of the lung, the bladder and the breast in adults exposed over many years.
"Polluted water and soil bring their own dangers too, linked to cancers of the liver and digestive system downstream of poorly regulated factories.
"So when we talk about preventing cancer, we cannot speak only of smoking and diet, important as those are.
"We must also speak honestly about what our factories release, what our vehicles put into our streets and what we allow to settle into the lungs of a sleeping child."
Sultan Nazrin said Malaysia must therefore consider how it balances economic growth with environmental safeguards.
Pointing to London as an example, he said stronger environmental regulation could produce measurable improvements in public health.
Following the introduction of its Ultra Low Emission Zone, which charges the most polluting vehicles high fees to enter the city centre, children in central London
experienced significant improvements in lung function as toxic vehicle emissions fell.
"Before the scheme began, children in central London had noticeably weaker lungs than children in Luton, a town near London.
"Within five years, as toxic exhaust fell sharply in London, those children's lungs recovered so well that they nearly caught up with children in Luton.
"The number of London children with poorly functioning lungs fell from about one in seven to about one in 11.
"Damage many once thought was simply the price of city life turned out not to be permanent.
"Clean the air, and children's bodies can heal."
Sultan Nazrin said the lesson from London was a hopeful one.
"Pollution and disease are not simply facts of modern life we must accept. They are the result of choices, and choices can be changed.

"If a city as large as London can restore its children's lungs within five years, then Malaysia, blessed with rainforest, coastline and industries still young enough to build cleanly from the start, can protect the lungs and the futures of our own children."
He said addressing the issue was not a task for the Health Ministry alone, but required action across the environmental, transport and industrial sectors.

"It belongs equally to those responsible for our environment, our transport, our industry and business leaders, who must help weigh the cost of cleaner production against a cost that cannot be priced: a child's life.

"I say this not to single out any one sector, but because I believe Malaysia's industries, given the chance to lead on this, will find that cleaner growth and competitive growth need not be different things."

Present were Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah, National Cancer Society Malaysia president Datuk Dr Saunthari Somasundaram and Health Ministry deputy director-general (public health) Dr Ismuni Bohari.

1fb27e4ffeade16d: DHAKA: Thousands of opposition supporters launched a long march across Bangladesh on Saturday, piling pressure on prime minister Tarique Rahman's government over acute shortages of cooking gas, electricity, and fertiliser.
The action marks the first major street mobilisation against the government, which came to power in the South Asian country of 170 million people six months ago.
Waving banners and chanting slogans, crowds gathered at a public square in Dhaka before setting off on the first leg of a march to the port city of Chittagong, with rallies planned along the route.
"This movement is aimed at ensuring cooking gas and lighting up every household with electricity," opposition leader Shafiqur Rahman told supporters.
Bangladesh has been reeling from acute shortages, partly caused by the war in the Middle East, while questions have been raised over the government’s handling of the crisis.

The rally comes a day after the arrest of a college student who allegedly insulted senior government officials while venting frustration over high electricity bills, a move critics said reflected growing intolerance of dissent.

af62504f185dbdca: PETALING JAYA: DAP MP Ramkarpal Singh has hit out at a PAS assemblyman from Kedah for questioning the timing of DAP urging the attorney-general to review the 47 charges faced by Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

Pengkalan Kundor assemblyman Mardhiyyah Johari said yesterday the issue was not raised when DAP and its allies in Pakatan Harapan needed Umno’s support to form the federal government after the 2022 general election.
Ramkarpal, who is the Bukit Gelugor MP, said Mardhiyyah “is clearly erroneous and ignorant of DAP’s stand on the matter”.

He said that if she had checked the facts, it would have become clear that DAP had raised serious concerns over the matter immediately after the High Court granted Zahid a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) on Sept 4, 2023, following the prosecution's application.
He pointed out that DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook issued a statement the very next day, calling for the AG to explain his decision.

“Loke had then said that DAP will always uphold the principle of separation of powers between judicial, executive and legislative branches and ensure there is no executive intervention in any court case, before pointing out that the issue was of public interest,” he said.

Ramkarpal, who is DAP’s legal bureau chairman, said the party had also urged the Attorney-General's Chambers to explain why it had decided to take no further action against Zahid, as stated in its statement dated Jan 7 this year.

He also said that on Jan 8, he asked the AGC why it had suddenly taken the view that the High Court’s prima facie findings against Zahid did not carry weight, particularly when those findings were based on evidence presented in court by the prosecution itself.

Ramkarpal said the party will continue asking questions about the AG's decision in Zahid’s case “as it clearly makes no sense”, especially since the High Court had made prima facie findings against him.
“The question that arises instead is whether PAS will do the same or refrain from doing so, now that Umno and PAS seem to enjoy a cosy relationship with each other,” he said.
On Thursday, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer urged the attorney-general to review Zahid's case, with DAP Youth backing the call the following day.
Zahid, who is also the deputy prime minister, was granted a DNAA on 47 charges involving corruption, money laundering and criminal breach of trust in the Yayasan Akalbudi case.

15fe8f767ae2cb3f: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) decision to stop requiring suspects to wear its orange uniform during remand proceedings is appropriate, but the policy must be applied equally regardless of a person's status, wealth or political position, said a criminologist.

Dr Haezreena Begum Abdul Hamid said the key issue was ensuring that investigation and punishment remained distinct, as a person brought before a court for remand was still a suspect and had not been found guilty.

"I think the main point here is that we need to separate investigation from punishment. When someone is brought to court for remand, that person is still a suspect. The court is not deciding guilt at that stage.
"So, in that sense, removing the orange uniform is appropriate. My only concern is that the policy must be clear and applied consistently," she told the New Straits Times.

Haezreena said allowing suspects to appear in civilian clothing could also reinforce the presumption of innocence, particularly given the strong visual association between the orange uniform and criminality.
"The problem with the orange uniform is that once you see someone wearing it, particularly in a photograph, you immediately associate that person with criminality.
"But this person may only be under investigation. So civilian clothing better reflects where they actually are in the criminal justice process."
However, she cautioned that the move could undermine public confidence if there appeared to be different standards for ordinary suspects and prominent individuals.
"In my opinion, the bigger issue is not really the orange uniform. It is whether everybody is treated the same.
"If an ordinary person is brought to court in orange and handcuffs, but a politician or prominent
businessman comes in civilian clothes without restraints, naturally people are going to question this double standard.
"That is where public confidence can be affected," she said.
Haezreena said MACC should introduce a clear written policy governing clothing and the use of restraints, with any differences in treatment based solely on objective considerations.
"If there is a reason for different treatment — security, escape risk or some operational concern — then there should be an objective reason for it.
"Status, wealth or political position should have nothing to do with it," she said.

She said the previous practice of suspects appearing publicly in distinctive orange clothing could also have lasting reputational and psychological consequences, even if they were subsequently not charged or were acquitted.
"Once someone's photograph in that orange uniform is everywhere, that image stays with them even if they are eventually not charged or are acquitted.

"From a criminological perspective, there is also labelling theory. Once society starts seeing you as a criminal, that label can follow you into your work, family and social life even if you are never convicted," she said.
Haezreena said the change could also affect media coverage of corruption cases, as images of suspects in orange uniforms could sometimes overshadow the substance of court proceedings.
"Civilian clothing may reduce that visual impression of guilt and hopefully shift the attention back to the investigation and the court proceedings," she said.
On the use of handcuffs, Haezreena said restraints should neither be imposed automatically on every arrested person nor waived simply because a suspect was prominent.
She said factors such as the risk of escape, violence, previous resistance and potential danger to the suspect or others should instead determine whether restraints were necessary.
"I don't think security and dignity are incompatible. MACC obviously has to maintain custody and ensure that someone doesn't escape or pose a danger," she said.

The NFL will never turn itself off, so it’s on fans to do so As a new NFL season begins this Wednesday, the danger of America’s most-watched sport has never been more clear. A new and widely circulated study published in the British Journal of Medicine examined the donated brains of former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 and compared them with the overall number of players who died during that period. Of the 235 donated brains in that period, 215 had evidence of the degenerative brain condition chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE). That group of 215 comprised 24.5% of the former players who died during that period in total. Given the finding, the study’s authors estimate that the prevalence of CTE among players who died in that period was at minimum 24.5% to a maximum of 97.7%, with the actual rate likely somewhere in between. 39b0c55ea9c0934f: KOTA BARU: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that a representative of the United States (US) Embassy once asked him about the party's proposed candidate for prime minister during a meeting at the US Embassy in Malaysia.
Hadi said the question was raised after two senior Pas leaders, Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and Datuk Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, had earlier met the US ambassador.
"He asked, 'Who does Pas propose as prime minister?' I said, 'Who does America (United States) agree with?'
"The meeting took place when Pas was still part of the Pakatan Rakyat coalition, during the visit of US President Barack Obama to Malaysia," he said.
He said this during his winding-up speech at the 72nd Pas Annual Muktamar here yesterday.
Hadi said Takiyuddin and Samsuri, who was then his political chief, had gone to the US Embassy to meet the ambassador after the meeting was arranged.
He further claimed that during the meeting, the two Pas leaders were informed of the possibility of bringing down the government and taking over the administration.
Hadi also alleged that the US was prepared to assist in the effort.
"However, Takiyuddin and Samsuri remained steadfast and were not influenced by the offer. Both our men remained steadfast. They were not influenced," he said.
Hadi said following the meeting, the US ambassador requested to meet him, and he attended the meeting with Datuk Mustafa Ali.
He said the question of a potential prime minister was also raised during the meeting, but he did not regard it as a priority as a decision would only need to be made when the time came.
"At that time, the Americans asked who the candidate they supported was, and the name of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad was mentioned and received a positive response from them.
"I told them Mahathir. Mahathir? 'That's good,' he replied. Why fuss over who it would be? When the time comes, there will be someone. What is important is that we do our work.
"This is what is important. We resolve the divisions, resolve the crisis. Go back and work, go back and carry out our duties," he said.

f479601a9b23c317: JAKARTA: Thick smog has blanketed parts of Indonesia as the vast archipelago for weeks battles to contain fires that have burned large swathes of Borneo and Sumatra.
The hazardous smoke has led to an increase in respiratory problems, forced schools to close, and has been drifting to neighbouring countries including – Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.
Here's what to know:
WHERE ARE THE FIRES?
Most of the fires are concentrated on Borneo island, home to vast tropical jungle that Indonesia shares with Brunei and Malaysia, as well as Sumatra.
So far this year, nearly 300,000 hectares of land have burned in Indonesia, according to an independent estimate from the Nusantara Atlas portal.

Indonesia saw an uptick in carbon emissions since late July, and by the end of last month the levels were comparable to previous El Nino years of 2015 and 2019, Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) senior scientist Mark Parrington told AFP.

"We're seeing already now... really extreme fire emissions comparable to those previous strong El Nino years, and also the extent of the smoke and the haze and the air quality impacts," Parrington said.
Fires in the archipelago have released more than 23 million metric tons of carbon emissions between August 28 and September 3, according to CAMS' Fire Emission Watch portal.
It was higher than 20.7 million metric tons of emissions from fires over the same period in 2015, which was a strong El Nino year.
WHAT CAUSES THE FIRES?

Analysts said that the El Nino weather phenomenon, which the United Nations said this week could turn out to be the strongest in four decades, has contributed to creating drier conditions in Indonesia and made it easier for fires to spread.
But slash-and-burn land-clearing practices also contributed to the damage, said David Gaveau, founder of the Nusantara Atlas.
"El Nino does not ignite fires. It creates the dry conditions that allow human-started fires to escape and become very large," he told AFP.
The fires are difficult to extinguish because many occurred on peatlands, a wetland ecosystem with layers of partially decomposed organic materials that become flammable when dry.
Between January and August this year, more than 210,000 hotspots were detected in peatland areas across the country, according to NGO Pantau Gambut.
"Peat is a naturally wet ecosystem and stores large amounts of organic material. When peat is drained, this organic material is converted into fuel," Pantau Gambut spokesman Wahyu Perdana said.
WHAT IS THE IMPACT?
More than five million people across Borneo and Sumatra are directly exposed to the health risks from haze, deputy health minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono said last month.
Over 1.4 million students were attending classes remotely, with many schools closed due to worsening air quality, an education ministry official said this week.
In Malaysia, soaring pollution levels prompted the government on Friday to declare an emergency in a region of the Sarawak state in Borneo, with nearly 650 schools closed next week.

In the Philippines, air quality was slowly returning to normal after a week of reaching "very unhealthy" and "severely unhealthy" PM 2.5 levels that saw officials shutter schools in cities and provinces citing the drifting haze.
The haze also drove air quality in Singapore's central region to an "unhealthy" level on Friday, the country's National Environment Agency data showed.

875fdf64a90bb6c5: SAN FRANCISCO, Sept 5 — The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said Friday that it has opened an investigation into Tesla’s certification that its new Cybercab meets all applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS), reported Xinhua.

The agency said the inquiry will examine, among other issues, the extent to which Tesla’s certification depended on determinations that certain FMVSS are inapplicable to the Cybercab.

In the United States, the NHTSA establishes vehicle performance requirements, while automakers must certify that their vehicles meet applicable standards before entering the US market, subject to agency oversight to confirm compliance. The NHTSA said it conducts investigations when certified vehicles appear not to adhere to those requirements.

NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison said the agency fully supports the safe development and deployment of automated vehicles but stressed that as the federal regulator it must ensure that applicable laws are followed.

The NHTSA said it is in the process of overhauling federal vehicle safety standards and has begun work on eight rulemakings over the last year, including standards relating to brake pedals, windshield wipers, lighting and rearview mirrors.

Danish berkata hanya beberapa minggu lalu, Tuan Ibrahim mengingatkan PAS dan Umno bahawa tidak sepatutnya wujud konsep 'abang besar' atau 'adik kecil' dalam rundingan mereka, sebaliknya semua pihak perlu dilayan secara sama rata.
"Hari ini lain pula ceritanya. Bila mahu kerjasama dengan Umno, katanya jangan ada 'abang besar'.
"Bila mahu serang PKR, tiba-tiba Umno pula jadi 'abang besar'. Politik PAS ini ikut prinsip atau ikut musim," katanya.

Pada 16 Ogos lalu, Tuan Ibrahim berkata sebarang formula kerjasama antara PN dan Barisan Nasional (BN) bagi PRN Melaka perlu berasaskan kesamarataan dan tidak hanya tertumpu kepada pembahagian kerusi negeri.
“Kita tidak seharusnya menganggap sesiapa sebagai abang besar atau adik kecil,” katanya.

Semalam, Tuan Ibrahim berkata PKR tidak sepatutnya memberi kata dua kepada Umno sama ada mahu kekal dalam kerajaan perpaduan atau beralih menyokong PN, kerana PKR sendiri bergantung kepada kekuatan Umno.
Beliau berkata PKR perlu menyedari kedudukan serta jumlah kerusi Parlimen dan DUN dimilikinya berbanding Umno, sebelum mengeluarkan kenyataan berbentuk amaran kepada rakan dalam kerajaan.

Beliau mengulas desakan Naib Ketua Pemuda PKR Nabil Halimi supaya Umno menyuarakan pendirian dengan jelas sama ada mahu terus bersama kerajaan perpaduan atau beralih menyokong PN selepas Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi menyarankan PRU16 wajar diadakan lebih awal.

3fa7bd620b8082ba: BOGOTA: A guerrilla drone attack on a military garrison in Colombia killed at least two soldiers and wounded five others on Friday, authorities said.
President Abelardo de la Espriella, who has pledged to get tough on crime, blamed the country's largest active armed group, the National Liberation Army (ELN), for the attack.
"To the ELN I say with absolute clarity: for every police officer or soldier you kill, I will bring down on you the full weight and legitimate force of the State," he said on X.
The attack took place in Ocana, in the northeastern Catatumbo region, where De la Espriella's government is currently conducting military operations against guerrillas.
A military source in the region told AFP that at least 20 drones loaded with explosives were used.
Colombia is the world's largest cocaine producer and is grappling with its worst violence in a decade.
Since taking office, De la Espriella has stepped up bombings and ground operations against armed groups.
Colombia has also joined the Shield of the Americas, US president Donald Trump's anti-cartel alliance of Latin American countries including Argentina, Ecuador and El Salvador.
De la Espriella is set to receive US state secretary Marco Rubio in the Caribbean city of Barranquilla next week.
88cff929b898225a: WASHINGTON, Sept 5 —The United States (US) will not grant birthright citizenship to children of foreign government employees born in the US if neither parent is a US citizens, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said in a document, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.

98a5ad58550bea00: KUANTAN: Kafe Secangkir in Sungai Karang Darat here, which was run by the late Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, closed its doors yesterday and will be handed over to a new tenant.

He said some customers arrived as early as 9.30am, reflecting their continued support for the café from the day it opened until its final day.
"I appreciate the presence, support and patience of everyone who came to the café during its operating hours, from 3pm to 9pm yesterday.

c385cf4a9b360ca0: KUALA LUMPUR: Six areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy air quality, with Serian registering the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 287 as of 1pm today.
No areas recorded hazardous air quality.

Department of Environment deputy director-general (development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the six areas were Serian (287), Kuching (267), Samarahan (242), Sri Aman (251), Samalaju (202) and Bintulu (201).
She said 25 other areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, while 26 recorded moderate readings and 11 recorded good air quality.
"Among the areas recording unhealthy readings were several locations in Johor, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, Sabah, Sarawak and Selangor.
"In Sarawak, Limbang recorded an API reading of 160, Miri (182), Mukah (188), Kapit (151), Sibu (172) and Sarikei (179)," she said in a statement.
She said the readings were recorded amid continuing dry weather conditions across parts of the southern Asean region.
"The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) detected 139 hotspots in Kalimantan, 138 in Sumatra and 16 in Malaysia as of Sept 4.
"Of the Malaysian hotspots, five were detected in Sabah, nine in Sarawak and two in Terengganu.
"The ASMC also reported moderate to dense haze moving northeastwards from Kalimantan towards parts of Sarawak, Sabah and Brunei."

Moderate to dense smoke was also observed over North and East Kalimantan, as well as central and southern Sumatra, while moderate haze was reported over Singapore, southern Peninsular Malaysia and eastern Java.

cee5d8019c861713: MELAKA: The Melaka government will study a proposal to make the state one of the earliest in Malaysia to set a basic salary of between RM2,500 and RM2,800 before submitting its recommendation to the Federal Government.

ff18c53a382ec604: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Manchester United’s enduring global appeal was on full display at the Malaysia Airlines Pavilion at the Malaysian Association of Tour and Travel Agents (Matta) Fair 2026 today, with more than 500 fans turning up to meet club legends Park Ji-sung, Wes Brown and Edwin van der Sar.
The event not only drew supporters from across Malaysia but also fans who travelled from overseas, a testament to the English Premier League giants’ worldwide following.

Among them was avid Red Devils memorabilia collector Adam Schwereb, 52, from Sydney, who flew into Malaysia to attend the event and meet the Manchester United legends, an opportunity he described as “too good to be missed”.

“I flew in last Wednesday to come to Matta Fair. It’s always a good opportunity, coming in from down south to catch up with the boys. And it’s Manchester United; we travel the world for it,” he told Bernama on the sidelines of the fair here.

Schwereb, who has attended matches at Old Trafford on several occasions, said events such as this provided supporters who could not travel to England with a rare opportunity to meet their footballing heroes in person.
The lifelong supporter said the initiative was particularly meaningful for younger fans who could now meet players who had played a key role in Manchester United’s decorated history.
He also revealed that the trip would add two prized pieces to his personal Manchester United collection, with items from Park and Van der Sar becoming part of his museum in Sydney.
Young Vietnamese fan Nguyen Danh Truong, 12, was among the foreign fans at the event, travelling from Ho Chi Minh City to Malaysia with his father Nguyen Van Tai.
Truong, who is spending three days in Malaysia, said the meet-and-greet session was the sole reason his father planned the trip.

Meanwhile, Bryan Foong, chief executive officer of Airline Business at Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), the parent company of Malaysia Airlines, said the strong response from supporters reflected the strength of Manchester United’s fan base globally and the value of the airline’s partnership with the club.
“It’s very popular. A lot of people come. It also helps us to create the business and the buzz around Malaysia Airlines as well,” he said.

Foong said the airline’s three-year partnership with Manchester United, which began in 2023, had so far been particularly effective in boosting the national carrier’s visibility and market presence, given the club’s extensive fan base across markets it served.
“The fan base for Manchester United is huge, right? And for us, they’re important and spread out across the world.

“Wherever we are, in terms of where we fly to, like Australia, Southeast Asia, India and even to the United Kingdom, they’re very well received and the Manchester United fans are very loyal. So it’s a good partnership for us,” he said. — Bernama
58e6674bd5d5eb61: IPOH: Police detained four local men early yesterday morning in connection with two separate cable theft cases in Kampar and Kuala Kangsar.

Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the first arrest in Kampar was made at about 4.30am when a Malim Nawar Police Station patrol team spotted two men, aged 42 and 46, acting suspiciously at the Muniswarar Temple in Bata Malim Nawar.
He said the inspection resulted in the seizure of two cable cutters and five rolls of cable, which Telekom Malaysia (TM) technicians later confirmed belonged to the company.
"The telephone line cable had been cut and was no longer functioning, resulting in an estimated loss of about RM1,000 to TM," he said in a statement last night.
In a separate incident in Kuala Kangsar, he said police were alerted by members of the public at about 3am to the suspicious movement of two vehicles around Taman Sri Pagi, Kati.
Mohd Alwi said, acting on the information, a team from the Criminal Investigation Division of the Kuala Kangsar District Police Headquarters arrested two men, aged 24 and 36, along Jalan Raja Chulan.

Following the arrest, he said police seized a silver Toyota Vios, a cable cutter, a cable-pulling iron, three rolls of cable, a crossbody bag, a mobile phone and several other items believed to be linked to the case.
Mohd Alwi said checks revealed that all four suspects had previous records, including for drug-related offences.
He said both cases were being investigated under Section 379 of the Penal Code, with police also probing the suspects' possible involvement in other cable theft cases in the district.
d79835d0b2967d7b: KUALA LUMPUR: The first batch of United Sikhs Malaysia volunteers has arrived in Kathmandu on a humanitarian mission to assist families affected by the Nepal floods and support efforts to locate missing Malaysians.
The five-member Team A, led by Mandeep Singh and Pravin Nagapan, will be deployed for two weeks, while other teams remain on standby for the next phase.

United Sikhs Malaysia legal director Raspreet Kaur told the New Straits Times that the team's immediate priority was to reach vulnerable families, particularly those in underserved and hard-to-access areas.

"Our immediate objective is to reach vulnerable families, particularly in underserved and difficult-to-access areas, and provide practical humanitarian assistance to protect them from further hardship," she said.
The team will distribute essential supplies and temporary shelter materials to about 300 families while coordinating with local authorities and responders.
Mosquito nets and tarpaulins worth about RM28,000 have already arrived at a gurdwara in Kathmandu, while volunteers will source ropes and other essentials before heading to the affected areas.
Raspreet said Team A would assess access routes and ground conditions before entering the affected areas, while Teams B and C would remain on standby depending on needs on the ground.
"During this initial deployment, we will also assess urgent unmet needs and determine whether a larger or longer-term humanitarian response is required," she said.
The Nepal floods, which struck the Trishuli Valley near the border with China's Tibet region on Aug 26, have left more than 1,200 people dead and destroyed over 2,500 buildings.
More than 4,750 people remain missing across Nepal and Tibet.
Of the Malaysians affected, 77 have been located and brought to Kathmandu for repatriation, while 55 remain unaccounted for.
Meanwhile, the Smart team deployed to Nepal is expected to remain there for seven to 10 days as part of the humanitarian mission.
2141710f77fbf613: KUALA LUMPUR: Despite suffering horrific facial injuries in a crash at last month's Glasgow Commonwealth Games, national track rider Lau New Joe is back in the saddle and is determined to prove a point at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Sept 19-Oct 4.
New Joe suffered a heavy crash in the men's scratch race final in Glasgow and spent the night in hospital there.
He, however, returned to training just five days after the incident.
Armed with a new track bike from the National Sports Council (NSC) - his old one was written off in the crash - he is now undergoing final preparations for the Asiad.
The 21-year-old is an endurance rider and he will compete in the men's omnium in Nagoya.
"I want to make sure that I achieve all the targets set for me during each training session," said New Joe in a statement released by NSC today.
"When I am on the start line, I want to know that I have already done my best (in training)."
Malaysia has long produced top track sprinters including the likes of Josiah Ng, Rizal Tisin, Azizulhasni Awang, Fatehah Mustapa and more recently Shah Firdaus Sahrom and Izzah Izzati Asri.
New Joe is looking to show that Malaysia also has strong talent and potential in the endurance events.
"I want to show that track endurance also has a place in Malaysian cycling and that we also have strong potential," he added.
"Hopefully we can get more support for this event, similar to what has been extended to other events."
New Joe already knows what it is like to stand on the top step of the podium for Malaysia at a multi-sport games.
Together with teammates Hafiq Jafri, Azim Aliyas and Yusri Shaari, he helped Malaysia win the team pursuit gold at the Thailand SEA Games in December.
New Joe also won the points race silver in Bangkok.

e942afb5cf8c7979: KOTA BHARU: Presiden PAS Hadi Awang mendakwa parti itu pernah ditawarkan pihak asing untuk menjatuhkan kerajaan.
Katanya, perkara itu berlaku ketika lawatan bekas presiden Amerika Syarikat (AS), Barack Obama ke Malaysia pada 2014, apabila beberapa pemimpin PAS dijemput bertemu di Kedutaan AS.

“Kita atur Takiyuddin dengan Samsuri, setiausaha politik saya masa itu. Dia (pihak AS) nak ajak bincang, sanggup nak jatuh kerajaan, nak ambil alih kerajaan Amerika sanggup tolong,” Hadi berkata demikian ketika menceritakan pengalaman itu semasa ucapan penggulungan sempena Muktamar Tahunan PAS Ke-72 di Pusat Tarbiah Islamiah Kelantan (Putik).
Hadi berkata, dua pemimpin PAS berkenaan bagaimanapun tidak terpengaruh dengan tawaran tersebut dan kekal dengan pendirian parti untuk menolaknya.

"Wakil daripada kedutaan tanya, adakah PAS merancang menjatuhkan kerajaan Barisan Nasional (BN) pada masa itu? Jadi, kami tak tak bagi apa-apa keputusanlah kerana kita tidak mengharapkan 'interference' daripada negara luar.
"Sebab politik negara kita, negara kitalah, tak boleh campur tangan luar. Kalau parti lain nak campur tangan luar nak menjatuhkan itu ikut merekalah, kami tidak, kami tidak," katanya.
1cfebe14338490f6: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Sarawak has seen a slight drop in tourist arrivals amid the current haze, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.
He said the decline was expected to continue until the haze situation improved.

“There’s a little bit of drop in the number of tourist arrivals lately. 81532ead9775bfca: KUALA LUMPUR: Mixed doubles pair Goh Soon Huat-Shevon Lai may have fallen short of the China Masters final, but their encouraging run in Shenzhen has convinced them they are finally heading in the right direction.
The independent world No. 11 pair lost 21-11, 24-22 to China's world No. 1 Feng Yan Zhe-Huang Dong Ping in the semi-finals at the Shenzhen Arena on Saturday.
It was Soon Huat-Shevon's first Super 750 semi-final since the India Open in January last year and their first appearance in the last four this season after three consecutive second-round exits.
Shevon said they had struggled for direction in recent months but that working with a new coach had given them fresh impetus.
"In the past few months, we lost a bit of direction and lost our way in the process," said Shevon.
"We did not have a clear direction or goal. Now that we have been working with a new coach, there are new challenges that we have to face.
"It has also given us a refreshed environment that both of us can look forward to."
Soon Huat said their performances in Shenzhen showed their efforts were beginning to bear fruit.
"It means a lot to us because we can see plenty of improvement from both of us," he said.
"We will keep going and work harder."
Although Yan Zhe-Dong Ping dominated the opening game, Soon Huat-Shevon responded with a tactical adjustment in the second to push the Chinese pair to deuce.
Shevon said they changed their defensive approach after struggling to deal with Yan Zhe's smashes and the pair's quick follow-up attacks.
"We discussed having a different game plan and finding a defensive response that would make it harder for them to follow up," she said."
Soon Huat then found his rhythm and was more solid with his smashes. That also gave us greater confidence when defending."
Yan Zhe-Dong Ping will face Malaysia's Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing in Sunday's final.
8b5dbf095469f7b0: PETALING JAYA: PKR Youth information chief Danish Hairudin has hit out at PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man for defending Umno over its ultimatum for the party to either remain in the unity government or switch its support to Perikatan Nasional.
“Since when was PAS appointed as Umno’s spokesperson? Or does PAS now feel that it is bigger than Umno and can speak on Umno’s behalf?” Danish said in a statement.

78abcb740b124a58: BUTTERWORTH: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said her personal experiences of child abuse and loss had strengthened her commitment to improving caregiver support for working mothers.
Fadhlina said her second child was abused by a caregiver who hit the child on the legs while she was working as a lawyer with a demanding schedule.
"I felt very guilty because, as a working mother and a lawyer at that time, my work schedule was very tight.
"I had no choice but to send my child to a caregiver," she said in her speech at Himpunan Gala Pesona Kasih Madani here today.
She said the experience convinced her that caregivers must demonstrate greater commitment, have access to training opportunities and understand their responsibility towards the community.
Fadhlina, who has six children, said three of them had been placed under the care of caregivers, adding that finding suitable childcare was a major challenge for working mothers.

Her experience was compounded by the death of her fourth child from Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), which she said left her traumatised and forced her to confront the difficult choice of whether to continue working or care for her children herself.
"I had to think about whether to continue working or stop and take care of my children," she said.
Fadhlina said support from her extended family, particularly her siblings, had helped her cope while continuing to work.
She said the experience underscored the importance of building a wider childcare ecosystem that would give working mothers confidence that their children were safe and properly cared for.
"This is how caregivers support working mothers like us, who are constantly thinking about our children's safety while we work," she added.
Fadhlina also backed efforts to expand the Kasih Madani caregiver programme, saying trained and accredited caregivers could help strengthen child protection at the community level.
She said she had conveyed the importance of the programme to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and would seek its inclusion in next year's Budget to enable more women to receive support.
Fadhlina said child protection should extend beyond childcare centres to schools, with everyone in the community sharing responsibility for safeguarding children.
"It takes a village to raise a child," she said, stressing that caregivers, schools, policymakers, parents and community organisations all had a role to play in protecting
children.
She said expanding the number of trained caregivers would also contribute to women's empowerment by allowing mothers to work with greater peace of mind.

More than 230 home-based caregivers from Penang and Kedah were recognised today at Himpunan Gala Pesona Kasih Madani, marking their progress through training and professional development aimed at strengthening the quality of early childcare in their communities.
Since its launch in August last year, Kasih Madani has reached more than 1,000 caregivers across four states: Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah and Penang.

Managed by Merdeka Centre with the support of the Finance Ministry through Yayasan Sime Darby, Kasih Madani is a government-driven initiative aimed at strengthening Malaysia's childcare ecosystem by empowering and building the capacity of home-based and community caregivers.

Through programmes such as Kursus Rintis Asuhan Madani and Seminar Asuhan Madani, caregivers are equipped with the knowledge and skills to improve the quality and safety of the childcare they provide.

Around 200 participants have been selected for the Bimbingan Keterampilan Profesionalisasi Asuhan Madani Professionalisation Programme, which provides a pathway for caregivers to further develop their capabilities and professional standing.

dc7b6329e213cd0e: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 27 illegal snares were destroyed during the Integrated Khazanah Operation (OBK) at several wildlife crime hotspots in forests in Selangor and Perak recently.

The enforcement patrols were conducted from Aug 11 to 25 by the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan), General Operations Force (GOP), Marine Police Force (PPM), Perak State Parks Corporation and Selangor Forestry Department.
Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said the 27 snares comprised spring traps, wire loop snares and nylon loop snares.
"The figure does not include other traps and devices that were also found during the patrols.
"The type and size of snares used generally depend on the species of wildlife being targeted.

"Spring traps are commonly used to target wild boar, while wire and nylon loop snares can be used to target larger or smaller wildlife, depending on the diameter of the wire or rope and the size of the spring mechanism used," he said in a statement today.
He said, in theory, the larger the snare and spring mechanism used, the larger the wildlife that could potentially be caught.
He said that in some cases, snares might be set to target specific species such as tigers, but could also trap other wildlife passing through the area.
"Moreover, snares are often concealed and camouflaged with their surroundings to reduce the chances of detection.
"This puts non-target species at risk of serious injury or death if they become trapped and are not freed within a short period," he said.

Abdul Kadir said cooperation between agencies through continuous patrols and targeted enforcement was among the key preventive measures to protect wildlife and their habitats from encroachment by irresponsible individuals.
He said illegal snaring not only threatened wildlife species but also affected the flora and fauna that formed part of the country's natural heritage.
c3713287775497a4: SINGAPORE, Sept 5 — Singaporeans recruited into a long-running investment scheme in China were promised cheap luxury living and a share of Nanning’s economic boom, but some found themselves closely watched and pressured to recruit friends and relatives.

One Singaporean public servant, identified only as Alice, told The Straits Times she was taken on a five-day trip to Nanning in Guangxi back in March after a friend pitched it as an investment opportunity.
She said she was not allowed to explore the city alone, with someone accompanying her everywhere and even following her to the toilet.
During a city tour, she was told: “We cannot get out of the car at all.”

Alice said she was also made to attend mandatory sales sessions in a condominium unit fitted with CCTV cameras, where recruiters promoted the scheme as a way for Singaporeans to “ride the China wave”.
Potential investors were told they could recoup their money by recruiting others, with each new participant said to be worth about S$10,000 (RM31,900).
Participants were expected to pay between S$26,000 and S$50,000 (RM83,000 and RM159,600), although recruiters were vague about what the money was actually being invested in.
Alice said she eventually paid S$70 (RM223) as a “promise fee” after becoming frightened by what she described as a “cult-like” environment, fearing she would not be allowed to leave if she refused.
While earlier news reports referred to the case as suspected pyramid scheme activity, The Straits Times describes the operation as a Ponzi scheme linked to the 1040 Sunshine Project.
A Ponzi scheme typically uses money from newer participants to pay earlier ones, while a pyramid scheme relies primarily on recruiting new participants to generate returns.

Other Singaporeans interviewed by the newspaper described similar recruitment trips dating back to 2014, with promises that Nanning would become the “next Shenzhen” and that developments there would attract major tourism and investment.
The scheme has also ensnared people from Malaysia, Indonesia, Taiwan and China, according to the report.
The accounts emerged after Singapore authorities announced on Thursday that 52 Singaporeans had been detained in Guangxi over suspected involvement in pyramid scheme activities.
Singapore’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has urged citizens to exercise caution over schemes involving recruitment, large upfront payments or promises of unusually high returns.

136d20b4717e440b: KATHMANDU: Inspired by the "miracle" rescue of two hydropower workers, Nepal's emergency response teams were digging with new vigour Saturday through piles of debris as the death toll from the flooding disaster crossed 1,200.

The rescued pair were among hundreds of hydropower workers who went missing since a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through the China-Nepal border following a vast glacial and rock collapse on Aug 26.
So far, 1,294 bodies have been recovered in Nepal, according to the disaster agency, with 5,053 people missing.
In China, state media said 31 people had been killed and 531 were missing. That takes the overall death toll to 1,325 people, with 5,584 missing.
"We have been working since morning on search and rescue operations," Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP on Saturday.
Searches continued at the Trishuli 3A tunnel where the two men were rescued on Friday, as well as multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects destroyed by the floods.
"Work is also underway at the tunnels," Basnet said. "We don't have an update yet, but the work goes on."
The government initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels.
Rescuers called it a "miracle" after the two men, caked in mud, were pulled out alive after being trapped for nine days.
They were taken to hospital and are said to be in a stable condition.
Experts from India, China, Australia and South Korea have been aiding Nepali rescuers in their search of survivors inside blocked tunnels.
With morgues overflowing, some 1,030 bodies hade been buried in mass graves after taking DNA samples for future identification by family members, Nepal Police said Saturday.
Prime minister Balendra Shah promised to provide "safe and comfortable accommodation" for thousands of people displaced by the disaster and currently living in temporary relief camps.
"We know that staying there (camps) is not easy for you," he said in an emotional post on social media late Friday.
"(But) we will once again create an environment where you can dream about and build your future," he said.
cbddfb0ed6731d9e: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — A total of six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at very unhealthy levels as of 1pm today with Serian recording the highest reading of 287.

“ASMC also reported that moderate to thick haze was observed moving northeast from Kalimantan to several areas in Sarawak, Sabah and Brunei.

“Moderate to thick smoke plumes were also observed in North Kalimantan and East Kalimantan as well as central and southern Sumatra, while moderate haze was observed in Singapore, the southern part of the Peninsula and eastern Java,” he said in a statement today.

65aca0ece4125e6f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Hani Othman, who has been in Nepal for eight days to follow the developments in the search for her missing Special Airborne Fire and Rescue Team (PASKUB) officer husband, today joined a mission to distribute humanitarian aid to disaster victims in the country, while hoping to find any clues as to her husband.

Mohd Fakhrul, 44, was reported missing after the four-wheel drive vehicle his group was in during an expedition to Everest Base Camp (EBC) was believed to have been affected by floods while in a valley in Rasuwa.

A total of 55 Malaysians have been reported as still unreachable following the disaster that occurred on August 26, while 77 others who were found safe in Tibet and Nepal have been brought to Kathmandu to undergo processing before returning to Malaysia.

de0373631a71814b: PETALING JAYA: Malaysia should amend its statutory rape law to protect teenagers in genuine consensual relationships from being prosecuted as sex offenders, a senior lawyer says.

Presenting his paper on “Decriminalising Adolescent Consensual Sex” at a law conference organised by the Selangor Bar Committee today, A Srimurugan said the law should distinguish between sexual exploitation and consensual relationships involving adolescents close in age.
Srimurugan said Section 375(g) of the Penal Code currently treats sexual intercourse with a girl below 16 as rape, regardless of consent.
This could result in a teenage boy being prosecuted for rape even where both parties were minors and the relationship was consensual.
“The rigid legal framework under Section 375(g) of the Penal Code fails to distinguish between exploitative acts and consensual adolescent behaviour,” he said.
Srimurugan said the problem arose particularly when parents discovered such relationships and lodged police reports against the teenage boys.
The law would then treat the girl as a victim and the boy as the offender, potentially exposing him to prosecution under the Penal Code and the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.

He proposed introducing a “Romeo and Juliet” or close-in-age exception, which would prevent criminal prosecution where adolescents engage in consensual sexual activity and there is no coercion, manipulation or force.
Under his proposed amendment, a male below 18 would not be guilty of rape for consensual sex with a person below 16, provided the relationship was voluntary.
The exception, however, would not apply where the male held a position of trust, power or authority over the younger person.
Srimurugan said such an approach would allow the law to protect children from predators while avoiding disproportionate punishment for adolescents involved in consensual relationships.
He stressed that decriminalising consensual sexual activity between adolescents would not encourage teenage sex.
He also proposed replacing criminal punishment with counselling and rehabilitation for both teenagers.
“A criminal conviction for rape can devastate a teen's life,” he said, pointing to possible consequences for education, scholarships, career prospects, and social functioning.
0ecd5acf73cb1f17: SEREMBAN, Sept 5 — All DNA samples from the next-of-kin of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for following floods and landslides in Nepal have been obtained, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said the samples would be sent to Nepal for the authorities there to conduct DNA matching, a process expected to take some time given the large number of victims involved.

Mohamad said the ministry received daily updates from the Chargé d’Affaires of the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu on the search operation and the situation on the ground, while the next-of-kin were also contacted regularly whenever there were new developments.

He said Nepal had limited the entry of foreign search and rescue (SAR) teams to avoid having too many teams on the ground, which could make it more difficult for the local authorities to coordinate the operation.

In another development, Mohamad said he would meet Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow in the capital on Monday to discuss efforts to enhance security in southern Thailand, as well as bilateral issues between the two countries.

Mohamad said peace in the region would benefit both countries, particularly by boosting Malaysia-Thailand border trade, which is of significant value.

2abe30e3fbaf3afd: SINGAPORE, Sept 5 — A Chinese national has been slapped with a record S$560,000 (RM1.74 million) fine for masterminding a scheme to smuggle nearly 30,000 bottles of duty-unpaid beer into Singapore.
Han Xiaoyang, 47, pled guilty yesterday to seven charges of fraudulently evading duty, Singapore-based news outlet CNA reported, citing information from the Customs Department.
“Investigations revealed that Han had conceived and orchestrated a scheme to import duty-unpaid beer from China into Singapore through false declarations,” Customs was quoted as saying.
But Han did not pay the fine and as such, will instead serve 164 days in jail in default.
The seven charges centred on his evasion of roughly S$60,127 (RM187,000) in duty on 28,236 bottles of beer.
According to the news report, judges also took into account 15 further charges, comprising four counts of duty evasion and 11 counts of evading Goods and Services Tax.
Han’s accomplice, 29-year-old countryman Tong Baobao, was sentenced separately in May for his role as general manager of Wan Changya International (WCI), the company used to run the operation.
Tong pled guilty to three counts of fraudulent duty evasion involving about S$39,517 (RM123,000) and was fined S$322,000 (RM1 million).
He too failed to pay and served 80 days in jail instead.
The scheme came apart on Nov 19 last year, when Customs officers raided an industrial unit along Tagore Lane and caught two workers unloading a liquor shipment.
That single consignment held 4,044 bottles of unpaid beer, and follow-up searches turned up a further 31,016 bottles stashed elsewhere.
“To carry out the scheme locally, he used a Singapore-incorporated company and directed Tong to act on his instructions,” Customs said.
Investigators found that Han told Tong in August last year of his plan to import duty-unpaid beer from China for storage and resale in Singapore, boosting profits by dodging tax.
Tong was instructed to get a China-based freight forwarder to misdeclare the beer as non-dutiable goods such as food items or industrial machinery.
Han bought the beer in China and shipped it to WCI in Singapore under those false declarations, after which Tong arranged for it to be warehoused and delivered to local buyers.
Singapore law provides a fine up to 20 times the evaded duty and a maximum jail term of one year for anyone convicted of dealing in duty-unpaid liquor.
28ea9a9d2078b6b0: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The historic Chew Jetty here was unaffected by a fire that broke out about 20 metres away and destroyed five business premises early this morning, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.

e919f6d4e7aef9b7: KATHMANDU: Angka korban akibat kejadian gelongsoran lumpur di Nepal melepasi 1,300, menurut polis Nepal, lapor Xinhua.

81a77f99034e39f9: SINGAPORE, Sept 5 — Singapore’s updated influenza vaccine for the Northern Hemisphere season will arrive about two weeks later than usual, as an industry-wide delay in vaccine production comes amid rising flu cases and demand for jabs.

The Ministry of Health (MOH) and Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA) said yesterday that supplies of the 2026-2027 Northern Hemisphere vaccine are expected to reach public and private healthcare providers in early to mid-October, Singapore-based news outlet CNA reported today.
The vaccine is typically available in Singapore by the end of September, ahead of the Northern Hemisphere flu season, which generally runs from October to March.
MOH and CDA said the delay was due to pharmaceutical companies taking longer to develop the latest vaccines, whose composition includes changes recommended by the World Health Organisation (WHO).
The delay comes as Singapore sees an increase in influenza cases, although the CDA said there was no indication that infections were more severe than usual.
Meanwhile, some clinics are already facing shortages of the current Southern Hemisphere vaccine as demand for flu jabs increases.
CNA found that three of 11 clinics contacted had run out of the Southern Hemisphere vaccine, while another said it had little stock left.

Healthway Medical, Raffles Medical and Parkway Shenton also reported increased demand for influenza vaccinations, with Healthway saying demand had risen steadily following the National Day long weekend.

The updated Northern Hemisphere vaccine is preferred for people at higher risk of severe influenza, including those aged 65 and above, children aged six months to under five years and people with underlying medical conditions, MOH and CDA said.

Those in these groups who have not received the 2026 Southern Hemisphere vaccine can consider getting it for interim protection, before receiving the Northern Hemisphere vaccine when it becomes available.
A minimum interval of eight weeks should be observed between the two doses, the authorities said.

For travellers heading to the US, Europe or Japan between December and February, Raffles Medical executive medical director Dr Chng Shih Kiat said the timing of vaccination would depend on their destination, travel date and health status.
He advised travellers to receive any influenza vaccine at least two weeks before their trip.
bd18c33b51d4356b: JAKARTA: An orangutan mother and her baby, threatened by encroaching wildfires to their habitat in Indonesia, were rescued earlier this week, authorities said in a statement Saturday.

The vast Southeast Asian archipelago has for weeks been fighting wildfires blanketing parts of Borneo and Sumatra with smog, with haze also contributing to air pollution in Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.
The orangutan pair had been under observation since July after being spotted in a plantation area near a forest in West Kalimantan, a local natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.

However, authorities decided to evacuate them to a rescue centre managed by the wildlife foundation Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) on Thursday as the fire spread near their habitat.
Their health is being closely monitored by veterinarians, but a preliminary check found no burn injuries on the two great apes.

"Exposure to smoke over a period of time... can affect the orangutan's respiratory system, especially when smoke concentrations in the habitat are very high," YIARI's veterinarian Komara, who like many Indonesians, uses only one name, said in a statement.
"Both individuals will continue to be monitored while they are at the rescue and rehabilitation centre," it said.

"The latest rescue means nine orangutans have been evacuated because of threats from wildfires in less than a month in the Ketapang district of West Kalimantan province," YIARI operational director Argitoe Ranting said.
"This shows that fires not only destroy forests but also deprive animals of shelter and food," Argitoe said.
Most animals "do not have many options" to relocate as their habitat burns, he added.

One orangutan died after being rescued last week, with a necropsy result pointing to smoke exposure as the cause of death, the West Kalimantan natural resources conservation agency said in a statement.

7f0321918d75f79a: KUALA LUMPUR: Enam kawasan Sarawak mencatatkan indeks pencemar udara (IPU) sangat tidak sihat setakat 1 tengah hari tadi dengan Serian merekodkan bacaan tertinggi, 287.

Beliau berkata, 25 kawasan mencatatkan bacaan IPU pada tahap tidak sihat melibatkan Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Pahang, Sabah, Labuan, Sarawak, dan Selangor, selain 26 kawasan mencatatkan status kualiti udara sederhana dan 11 kawasan pada tahap baik.
